name: Fascism
summary: Comparative scholarship defines the family by a revolutionary ultranationalism of national rebirth: a state and nation above the individual, a leader with a mass party, elitism, and a positive view of struggle, violence and war. It is defined by its negations of liberalism, communism and conservatism, subordinates the economy to the state while keeping private property, and divides on corporatism, religion, race and expansion.
scope: Fascism as a generic family, answered only from the defining scholarship: Payne's typological description (with Gentile's ten-point definition he quotes), Paxton's mobilizing passions, Griffin's palingenetic ultranationalism and Eco's Ur-Fascism (medium at most). The texts of Italian Fascism (Mussolini's Doctrine, Rocco) and of other member movements are not evidence here. Where the defining scholarship documents division (corporatism, religion, race, expansion) the answer is 0 low.

furtherReading.note: A readable essay on fourteen features of fascist thinking.

sources.author: Stanley G. Payne

sources.title: The Five Stages of Fascism
sources.author: Robert O. Paxton

sources.title: Staging the Nation's Rebirth (Griffin, in Fascism and Theatre)

sources.title: Ur-Fascism
sources.author: Umberto Eco, New York Review of Books
sources.usedFor: An essayist's list of fascist features (medium confidence at most).

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Payne says fascist movements subordinated economic issues to the state and the nation's well-being while retaining private property.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Payne describes the shared economic aim as ending the autonomy of large-scale capitalism under extensive government control and regulation.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Payne says fascist movements subordinated economic issues to the state, with extensive governmental control and regulation.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Gentile's definition (quoted by Payne) includes a corporative economy and Payne says most fascisms espoused corporatism, but German National Socialism explicitly rejected formal corporatism, so the family divides.

class-collaboration.rationale: Payne describes a multiclass, integrated economy and Gentile's definition seeks collaboration of the productive sectors, and Griffin says fascism rejected class conflict.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Payne lists rejection of economic determinism and anticommunism as defining, and Griffin says fascism rejected class conflict and all socialism.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Payne says fascist ideology rejected economic determinism, whether of Manchester or Marx, and Griffin says it rejected materialism.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Payne lists the fascist rejection of egalitarianism, and Griffin describes a vertical, anti-egalitarian model of democracy.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Paxton lists group duties superior to every right, universal or individual, Griffin says fascism repudiates universal rights, and Gentile's definition includes discrimination against groups seen as inferior.

universal-morality.rationale: Paxton says fascism rests on no formal philosophy with claims to universal validity, and Griffin says it repudiates Enlightenment rationalism.

strong-leader.rationale: The Fuhrerprinzip and a charismatic, personal style of command are in Payne's and Gentile's definitions, and Paxton and Griffin report authority concentrated in a national chieftain.

state-harmful.rationale: Payne says fascism sought a new nationalist authoritarian state, and Gentile's definition makes politics primary over the individual.

empower-police-military.rationale: Gentile's definition includes a police apparatus repressing dissent and a militarization of politics, and Payne lists military virtues as defining.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Paxton lists the primacy of the group with duties superior to every right, Payne defines fascist society as organic with the group taking precedence over individuals' rights, and Griffin says it repudiates individual responsibility.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Paxton's first mobilizing passion is duties to the group superior to every right, and Payne's organic view gives the group's role precedence over individual rights.

conscription.rationale: Payne lists militarization of politics and a mass party militia as defining, with war and military virtues normatized.

organic-representation.rationale: Gentile's definition makes the economy corporative, but Payne reports German National Socialism rejected corporatism and Gentile has a single state party, so the family is divided.

total-state.rationale: Gentile's definition has a totalitarian primacy of politics, though Payne cautions that fascist doctrine never projected complete totalitarianism.

more-religion-public.rationale: Payne calls fascism basically post-religious and secular, while Paxton says religion would play a larger role in some national variants.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Paxton places the nation's identity and community decline at the core, and Griffin says fascism seeks a national rebirth from the forces of decadence.

gradual-change.rationale: Payne calls fascism revolutionary ultranationalism and Griffin calls it anti-conservative and aimed at a new order.

nation-first.rationale: Payne and Griffin both define fascism as ultranationalism, and Payne lists a goal of radical change in the nation's relationship with other powers.

open-borders.rationale: Griffin says fascist nationality is defined in exclusive historical, cultural or ethnic categories, and Payne calls all fascist movements highly ethnicist.

revolution-justified.rationale: Payne defines fascism as revolutionary ultranationalism, and Griffin calls it a revolutionary force aiming at a new order.

natural-rulers.rationale: Payne makes extreme elitism part of the definition and Paxton lists the authority of natural leaders throughout society.

political-violence-never.rationale: Payne says fascism positively values violence as an end as well as a means, and Paxton and Griffin report redemptive and cathartic violence.

war-builds-character.rationale: Payne says fascism normatizes war and military virtues, and Paxton reports the beauty of violence and will in a Darwinian struggle.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Paxton lists the beauty of violence and will in a Darwinian struggle, and Payne names extreme social Darwinism.

military-superiority.rationale: Payne reports a goal of expansion or radical change in the nation's standing, with war and military virtues normatized.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Payne calls all fascist movements highly ethnicist, Gentile's definition makes the nation an ethnic and moral community, and Griffin has nationality in exclusive ethnic categories.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Paxton puts duty to the group above individual rights, Payne says fascism rejected materialism and prudential egotism, and Griffin says individuals subsume their personality in the community.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Payne and Griffin say fascism embraced modernity and often accelerated modernization, though Eco notes a rhetoric of rejecting the modern world.

restore-past-order.rationale: Payne says fascism was not a reversion to traditional values and Griffin says it was anti-traditional and aimed at a new order, though Eco stresses a cult of tradition.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Payne lists anticommunism as a defining negation and Griffin says fascism rejected all forms of socialism.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Payne says fascism values violence positively as end and means, Paxton reports redemptive violence, and Griffin reports violence as cathartic destruction.

independent-unions.rationale: Gentile's definition has the corporative economy suppressing trade union liberty.

workers-own-party.rationale: Gentile's definition has a single state party organising the masses, and Griffin says fascism rejects socialism.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Gentile's definition has the corporative organisation suppress trade union liberty and Payne says the movements eliminated the autonomy of labour organisations in the new economic structure.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Payne says the Marxist claim that fascism aimed to prevent changes in class relationships is not borne out by the movements themselves.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Payne lists anticommunism and a goal of ending large-scale capitalism's autonomy, with a new national corporatist or national socialist economy.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Payne calls fascism secular, post-religious and immanent.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Payne says fascism presupposed a secular, immanent frame of reference.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Gentile's definition gives the leader a sacred charisma, but Payne's secular, immanent fascism has no divine descent for rulers.

leader-cult.rationale: Gentile's definition crowns the hierarchy with a leader invested with sacred charisma, and Paxton and Griffin report the leader cult as characteristic.

democracy-best.rationale: Gentile's and Payne's definitions list anti-democracy and antiliberalism, and Griffin says fascism replaces horizontal democracy with a vertical one.

workers-councils.rationale: Gentile's definition has a single state party and a corporative economy, with Griffin saying fascism rejects socialism.

one-party-rule.rationale: Gentile's definition has a single state party leading mass mobilisation, though Payne notes the two fascist regimes began as coalitions and never fully escaped pluralist compromise.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Payne and Gentile report hierarchy, militarization and deference to the leader's command.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Gentile's definition has a police apparatus repressing dissent by organised terror, Paxton says victimhood justifies any action against internal enemies, and Griffin says persecution enforces uniformity.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Paxton says the group's victimhood justifies any action against its internal as well as external enemies, and Gentile includes persecution of those outside the community.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Gentile's definition has the regime destroying parliamentary democracy, Payne says fascists sought to transcend parliamentary cliquishness, and Griffin says it replaces horizontal democracy.

recall-officials.rationale: Gentile's definition has a hierarchy of functions named from the top.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Gentile's hierarchy is named from the top and Payne has leadership deferring to the leader rather than to members.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Griffin says fascism replaces horizontal democracy with a vertical one based on a new elite, and Eco says the Leader's power is not delegated democratically.

rule-by-example.rationale: Gentile's definition has a police apparatus and organised terror alongside the leader's command.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Gentile's definition and Payne's typology list expansion, but Payne finds some fascist movements defensive or uninterested in new empire.

defeat-communism.rationale: Payne and Griffin both list anticommunism and rejection of socialism as defining negations.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Eco says Ur-Fascism rests on an obsession with a plot, often international, and that Jews are the usual target as a group both inside and outside the nation; Paxton and Payne say nothing on a conspiring minority.

patriotic-education.rationale: Payne says fascism built a civic religion binding the nation in a common faith and loyalty, and Gentile's civil ethic requires total dedication to the national community.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Payne reports exaltation of youth and militarization of political style as defining, and Gentile reports the myth of youth with militarization as the model of life.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Gentile's definition has a warrior spirit and civic religion of the nation, and Eco reports a cult of heroic death.

sacred-nation.rationale: Payne reports a civic religion of the movement and nation, and Griffin treats fascism as a political religion of national rebirth.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Payne says fascists considered non-Europeans inferior and listed empire among their goals.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Paxton lists the group's primacy over every right and Payne lists military virtues as defining.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Payne lists military virtues, militarization and a party militia as defining.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Payne reports a willingness to use war, though some movements in satisfied states were defensive.

arms-reduction.rationale: Payne lists militarization and normatized war and military virtues as defining.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Payne's positive valuation of violence is incompatible with an absolute ban on killing.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Payne reports doctrines of inherent collective superiority of the nation.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Griffin lists rejection of materialism and Payne says fascism rejected materialism and prudential egotism.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Payne makes extreme stress on the masculine principle and male dominance defining, and Paxton lists natural leaders as always male.

women-suffrage.rationale: Paxton says fascist authority is that of natural leaders, always male.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Payne reports fascist male dominance and Paxton reports natural leaders as always male.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Payne says the fascist organic society made a place for women but gave the male's rights predominance.

clerical-rule.rationale: Payne says fascism is secular and post-religious.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Payne says fascism rests on idealism and vitalism against materialism, and Griffin treats it as a political religion.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Payne says fascism is vitalist and rejects rationalism, Griffin that it repudiates Enlightenment rationalism, and Eco calls it irrationalist.

national-rebirth.rationale: Payne's definition is revolutionary ultranationalism for national rebirth, Griffin's is palingenetic ultranationalism, and Paxton lists dread of decadence.

informal-organisation.rationale: Gentile's definition has a mass party and militia under a hierarchical leader, and Payne lists mass mobilisation and militarised organisation.
